_: THE ROOT LIST. One source, two consumers: shoot.mjs takes a preview of
every entry that needs one, build-hub.mjs writes ../index.html from the
same entries. Add a variation by adding a row and running both.
Same rule as 'aan test 4/tools/versions.json', which this file follows:
`what` and `settles` are NOT written from memory. Every line is lifted
from a document Alex wrote or from the page's own header comment, and
`source` names where. A made-up description on an index page is worse
than an empty one, because it reads as authoritative.
`opens` is a fact about the page, established by reading it, not a wish:
file    - double-click works; the page has no cross-origin dependency
server  - needs START.bat. External `<script type=module src=...>`,
bare specifiers behind Vite, or Astro's root-absolute paths
are all blocked or unresolvable on a file:// origin.
`shoot` is where the shooter loads it from. `reuse` instead means the
preview already exists and is copied, not re-taken - 'aan test 4' and
'aan test 6' already shot theirs at 1440x900 and there is no reason to

groups.title: Root
groups.blurb: The one page that carries its own everything - opens anywhere, needs nothing.

groups.title: aan test 2 — the concept page
groups.blurb: The page this whole shelf grew out of, plus the concept document it was argued from.

groups.title: aan test 4 — one hero, ten arguments
groups.blurb: Each version says the same things and only disagrees about how. Content never changes; index4 is the reference for copy, figures and links. Descriptions from aan test 4/docs/EXPERIMENT.md.

groups.title: aan test 5 — the Aperture
groups.blurb: A restart that rejected travel as the subject and proposed resolution instead. Implementation is stopped; index3 was rejected in full and is kept only as a failed experiment.

groups.title: aan test 1 — the terrain lab
groups.blurb: Not a design. A reusable Three.js / GSAP pipeline for a heavy terrain asset, plus throwaway presentation experiments on top of it. One Vite entry routes all nine by query parameter, so no mode pays for another's code.

groups.title: aan test 6 — Montfort mirror
groups.blurb: An offline 1:1 copy of mont-fort.com kept for studying its architecture, and the variant overlays built against it.

groups.title: aan test 3 — GD_LAB_TEST
groups.blurb: Its own git repository, one commit deep. Nothing has been built in it yet.

entries.name: index1_1
entries.what: The aan test 2 page built into a single 2.0 MB file — CSS, GSAP 3.15, Lenis, five AVIF plates and seventeen font faces all inlined as data URIs.
entries.settles: Whether the page can be handed to someone as one file that needs no server and no network. It can: zero requests leave the document.
entries.source: built 2026-09-03 from aan test 2 by tools/ in the scratchpad
entries.note: was GD2-concept-page.html until the hub took the index name

entries.name: aan test 2 / hero
entries.what: Summit act on AVIF plates, pinned for one viewport. Sky and mountain rise at differing rates; the near plate grows into a 34px blur instead of travelling out. Route drawn by scroll, two callouts opening at the fractions the descent meets them.
entries.settles: The source of index1_1 and of aan test 4/index9 — the version whose near-plane defocus was carried into both.
entries.note: loads GSAP by relative dynamic import, so file:// refuses it — index1_1 is this page made portable. Was aan test 2/index.html until that folder grew a portal of its own on 2026-09-03; the page itself is unchanged.

entries.name: aan test 2 / concept-page
entries.what: The 40 KB concept document rendered in the browser through marked.
entries.settles: Not a version — the written argument the versions are answers to.
entries.note: pulls marked from cdnjs, so it needs the network but not a server

entries.name: index1
entries.what: The production page. PNG hero, scrolled route, scene 2 in water.
entries.settles: The baseline. The design system was extracted from this one.
entries.note: was index.html until aan test 4's own hub took that name

entries.name: hero-v2
entries.what: index with three AVIF sources, nothing else.
entries.settles: What the AVIF plates cost the picture.

entries.name: index2
entries.what: index with the v2 footage cut.
entries.settles: Which ocean grade to ship.

entries.name: index3
entries.what: 3D mountain, full WebGL, route drawn on the terrain.
entries.settles: Can the PNG hero become real geometry without losing the scroll?
entries.note: the only captured route that is on the rock at every frame, and the only one that disappears and reappears

entries.name: index4
entries.what: Same as index3 with the second mountain (92-mountain).
entries.settles: Which of the two models carries the shot.
entries.note: identical module, different mesh, zero occlusion events — the route's quality is a property of the mesh, not the algorithm

entries.name: index5
entries.what: No canvas at all. Chaptered editorial, five acts, one pinned act.
entries.settles: Whether the page needs 3D to be good, or whether composition is enough.

entries.name: index6
entries.what: Scene 2 as a 2.5D ocean: flat plates over the real footage, depth from differing parallax rates.
entries.settles: Whether the WebGL diver is worth 900KB of three plus a 3.3MB rig.

entries.name: index7
entries.what: The vault reading. Navy alternating with a warm neutral, one governing event on the first screen, the record published as a plate. No canvas, no video, no scroll-driven anything.
entries.settles: Whether the direction holds when every structural decision has to name the vault entry it comes from — and whether the page still has to be dark.
entries.note: the only version that broke free of the client comp's metaphor

entries.name: index8
entries.what: index without the diver. Ships no three.js and no 3.3MB rig at all.
entries.settles: Whether the swimmer in scene 2 ever earned the frame.
entries.note: its header records the previous author's judgement: "index is the strongest of the seven"

entries.name: index9
entries.what: The GD_LAB_TEST hero brought in whole — its own palette, its own tokens, Lenis under the scroll. The near plate leaves by growing into blur instead of travelling out.
entries.settles: Whether a near plane should defocus rather than leave: the frame goes soft instead of emptying, so the next scene has something to emerge from.
entries.note: self-contained in assets9/, fonts repointed to the local faces

entries.name: Design system
entries.what: The tokens, the seven type ranks and the measured contrast table, computed from the live CSS at load.
entries.settles: Not a version — the rulebook every version above is judged against.

entries.name: index1
entries.what: First build of the Aperture architecture: intro, mountain hold, path to summit, callouts, ridge occlusion, then the takeover into water.
entries.settles: Whether resolution rather than travel can carry the scroll story.

entries.name: index2
entries.what: Second pass, captured in two states — clean, and with the path drawn.
entries.settles: Whether the path belongs on this composition at all. The with-path variant is filed REJECTED.

entries.name: index3
entries.what: Rejected in full as a visual direction. Kept only as a failed experiment — not to be polished, re-parameterised, renamed, or used as a base.
entries.settles: Grounds recorded verbatim: a white cable over a mountain instead of a path integrated with terrain; oversized dots resembling editing handles; disconnected route fragments; random callout placement; blur concealing weak composition; two scene panels with a visible boundary; a technical implementation more developed than its visual judgement.

entries.name: proto / hero-proof
entries.what: H1/H2 hero proof on a 700vh spacer. Type lives in the negative space, never on the peak.
entries.settles: Where the headline can sit once the peak owns the centre of the frame.
entries.note: pulls its faces from Google Fonts, so it wants the network

entries.name: / — inspection viewer
entries.what: Neutral technical viewer — OrbitControls, debug readout, wireframe toggle, Top/Oblique/Low cameras. The reference for judging the asset itself.
entries.settles: The terrain as delivered: 227,799 vertices, 450,000 triangles, normalised to a 20-unit span.

entries.name: ?cinematic=1
entries.what: 300vh scroll, pinned WebGL stage, one scrubbed GSAP timeline driving the whole camera move, HTML typography over the canvas.
entries.settles: Temporary motion study. Its scrim strength is derived from measured contrast against the terrain's brightest region, not chosen by eye.

entries.name: ?typeLab=1
entries.what: Giant "GD" as real TextGeometry placed onto the terrain by raycasting. Three treatments (Inlay / Monolith / Beacon), full control panel, slow auto camera.
entries.settles: Whether type can sit in the landscape as geometry rather than over it as HTML.
entries.note: its typeface JSON is generated from a licensed system font and must be regenerated from an OFL face before anything ships

entries.name: ?mountainLab=1
entries.what: Loads the 12 Unreal-derived mountains from one GLB with named nodes, arranges them as a foreground/midground/background corridor, plays a 2.5s assembly on load, then hands the camera to scroll.
entries.settles: The approved 12-mountain composition. No clouds, no ocean, no diver, no colour grading.

entries.name: ?mountainLabV2=1
entries.what: A deliberate break from V1, not a patch on it. Real scanned ground: the 450k-triangle photogrammetry landscape with 2K albedo/normal/AO, used instead of V1's procedural plane.
entries.settles: Whether real erosion and albedo variation fix the white carpet that every attempt to patch V1's floor produced.

entries.name: ?mountainMaterialTest=1
entries.what: Shows the approved 12-mountain composition and switches between the borrowed Unreal materials baked into the GLB and a new world-space triplanar rock/snow material.
entries.settles: Whether the borrowed materials can be replaced. No man, no route, no landing copy, no ocean.
entries.note: does not currently run: it reads CFG.scene.key.direction, and mountain-composition.js now describes the key light as azimuth/elevation. Verified 2026-09-03 — the preview is the loading state, which is as far as the page gets.

entries.name: ?manScroll=1
entries.what: One feeling: you were standing beside this person, and then you found out how big the world around him is. GSAP owns one scrubbed value driving camera, look-at and FOV; the rig owns bones on frame delta. GSAP never touches a bone.
entries.settles: The mechanical baseline for the character reveal.

entries.name: ?manScrollArt=1
entries.what: Art-direction experiment on the same mechanics. Everything reusable is imported, never edited — loadTerrain, CharacterRig, the placement and the scrub pattern.
entries.settles: What art direction alone changes, with the mechanics held identical to manScroll.

entries.name: ?manTest=1
entries.what: Drops the Fab "Survival Character FREE" onto the normalised terrain to judge visual quality, scale and pose. Transforms split three ways — placement, facing, and the rig's own bones — so a camera pass and the idle can never overwrite each other.
entries.settles: Human scale against the terrain. Not part of any design.

entries.name: Оригинал Montfort
entries.what: Untouched mirror of mont-fort.com. 33 pages, ~260 MB, URL structure kept 1:1 so every /_astro/ and /assets/ path resolves without rewriting.
entries.settles: The base every variant is an overlay on.

entries.name: Проба пера
entries.what: First variant — palette work. A variant is an overlay, not a copy: only changed files live in variants/01-proba/, the rest is served from the base.
entries.settles: Whether the mirror's architecture survives being re-coloured.

entries.name: GD_LAB_TEST
entries.what: Vite's own starter template, untouched — the counter button and the Vite and JavaScript logos. three and gsap are in package.json; nothing imports them.
entries.settles: not recorded
entries.source: aan test 3/GD_LAB_TEST/src/main.js and its single commit, 6ad6e2e "Initialize Vite 3D lab"
entries.note: no node_modules and no preview: it cannot be served without an npm install, and it is a scaffold rather than a version. Not the published GD_LAB_TEST that aan test 4/index9 was mirrored from.
